title: Describing people
goal: Say what people look like and what they are like, with adjectives that agree in gender and number.

items.en: adjective agreement: add -e for feminine, -s for plural

drills.prompt: Mei is kind. Which is correct?
drills.explain: gentil doubles the l in the feminine: gentille.

items.fr: un ami drôle / un petit garçon
items.en: adjective position: most go after the noun, a few short ones before

drills.prompt: How do you say “a shy friend” (a woman)?
drills.explain: Most adjectives go after the noun: une amie timide.

drills.prompt: How do you say “my younger sister”?
drills.explain: petit is one of the few adjectives that go before the noun. Before sœur it also means “younger”.

items.en: What is he like? (looks or personality)

blocks.title: Mei will meet Lucie's family this weekend
blocks.context: Mei asks her friend Lucie about her family.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Ta famille est comment ? Ton frère Thomas, il est comment ?
lines.en: What's your family like? Your brother Thomas, what's he like?

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Thomas ? Il est grand et brun. Il est très sympa, et drôle aussi !
lines.en: Thomas? He's tall and dark-haired. He's really nice, and funny too!

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Ma sœur est petite et blonde. Elle est un peu timide, mais elle est très gentille.
lines.en: My sister is short and blond. She's a bit shy, but she's very kind.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Mon père est sérieux, mais ma mère est très drôle. Ils sont âgés maintenant : mon père a quatre-vingts ans !
lines.en: My father is serious, but my mother is very funny. They're elderly now: my father is eighty!

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Et mon petit frère, Théo, il est jeune : il a vingt-cinq ans.
lines.en: And my younger brother, Théo, is young: he's twenty-five.

blocks.body: Two handy words in the dialogue: [[très]] = *very*, and [[un peu]] = *a bit*. They go right before the adjective: [[très gentille]], [[un peu timide]].

blocks.title: The adjective follows the person
blocks.body:
A French adjective changes to match the person it describes:

- **feminine**: add **-e** → [[grand]] → [[grande]]
- **plural**: add **-s** → [[grand]] → [[grands]], [[grandes]]

If the masculine already ends in **-e**, nothing changes for the feminine: [[jeune]], [[drôle]], [[timide]]. A group of men, or of men and women together, takes the masculine plural: [[Mes parents sont grands.]]

blocks.note: Two special patterns: [[gentil]] doubles the l ([[gentille]]), and [[-eux]] becomes [[-euse]]. Words ending in -x don't add -s: [[sérieux]] stays [[sérieux]].

blocks.title: Describing someone
blocks.note: Ask [[Il est comment ?]] / [[Elle est comment ?]] to mean *What is he / she like?*

examples.fr: Mes enfants sont un peu timides.
examples.en: My children are a bit shy.

examples.fr: Ma mère et ma sœur sont blondes.
examples.en: My mother and my sister are blond.

blocks.title: Where does the adjective go?
blocks.body:
With a noun, **most adjectives go after it**, the opposite of English:

- [[un ami drôle]] = a funny friend
- [[une femme sérieuse]] = a serious woman
- [[une fille timide]] = a shy girl

A few short, very common adjectives go **before** the noun. For now, just recognise them: [[grand]], [[petit]], [[jeune]], [[beau]] (beautiful, handsome), [[bon]] (good).

- [[un petit garçon]] = a little boy
- [[une jeune femme]] = a young woman
- [[un bon ami]] = a good friend

You will practise this order more later. After [[être]], there is no problem: [[Il est petit.]]

The feminine **-e** is silent, but it makes the consonant before it **heard**:

- [[grand]] ends in a nasal vowel; [[grande]] ends with a *d* sound.
- [[petit]] → [[petite]]: you hear the *t*.
- [[blond]] → [[blonde]]: you hear the *d*.
- [[brun]] (nasal) → [[brune]]: the nasal disappears and you hear *ü-n*.
- [[gentil]] (*zhan-tee*) → [[gentille]] (*zhan-tee-y*).
- [[sérieux]] → [[sérieuse]]: a *z* sound appears.

The plural **-s** is silent: [[grand]] and [[grands]] sound the same.

examples.fr: Il est petit. — Elle est petite.
Il est brun. — Elle est brune.

blocks.title: Big brother, little sister
blocks.body:
Before a family word, [[grand]] and [[petit]] usually mean **older** and **younger**, not tall and short:

- [[mon grand frère]] = my older (big) brother
- [[ma petite sœur]] = my younger (little) sister

So [[Mon petit frère est grand]] makes perfect sense: *My younger brother is tall.*

- **Forgetting the feminine:** [[Ma mère est grand]] → [[Ma mère est grande]].
- **gentil for a woman:** [[Elle est gentil]] → [[Elle est gentille]].
- **Plural sympa:** [[Ils sont sympa]] → [[Ils sont sympas]].
- **English order:** [[un drôle ami]] → [[un ami drôle]].
- **old:** for people, [[âgé]] is the more polite word. [[Vieux]] (old) is normal for things, but said of a person it can sound blunt.

In Québec you will often hear [[fin]] / [[fine]] meaning *kind, nice*: [[Ton père est fin !]] = Your dad is nice! In France, [[fin]] mostly means *thin* or *fine*. Recognise it, and use [[gentil]] yourself: everyone understands it.

examples.fr: Elle est vraiment fine, ta sœur.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Exaggerate the final consonant in the feminine forms.

lines.fr: Il est grand. Elle est grande.
Il est gentil. Elle est gentille.
lines.tip: gentille ends in a y sound.

lines.fr: Mon père est sérieux. Ma mère est sérieuse.
lines.en: My father is serious. My mother is serious.
lines.tip: sérieuse ends in a z sound.

lines.fr: Ma sœur est petite et brune.
lines.en: My sister is short and dark-haired.

lines.tip: The s of sympas is silent.

blocks.prompt: Who is the speaker talking about?
blocks.explain: No *y* sound at the end: [[gentil]], masculine. Feminine [[gentille]] ends in *ee-y*.
[[sont]] = several people, and the *d* sound in [[grandes]] = feminine.

blocks.explain: petit goes before frère (= younger). Age uses avoir: [[il a vingt ans]].
sérieux → sérieuse; drôle already ends in -e, so it doesn't change.

blocks.prompt: Raj and Karim are nice. Which is correct?
optionFeedback: Two people: the adjective needs a plural -s.

blocks.prompt: A friend asks about someone in your family: “Il est comment ?” or “Elle est comment ?” Describe that person: who they are, what they look like, and what they are like.
checklist: Who it is: C'est mon / ma …
Two adjectives for appearance (grand, petit, blond, brun…)
Two adjectives for personality, with très or un peu

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: C'est ma sœur, Sofia. Elle est petite et brune. Elle est très drôle et un peu timide. Elle est jeune : elle a vingt-deux ans.
models.en: This is my sister, Sofia. She's short and dark-haired. She's very funny and a bit shy. She's young: she's twenty-two.

blocks.prompt: Describe two people in your life (one man and one woman, or a group). Say what they look like and what they are like.
checklist: Describe a man and a woman (or a group)
Use at least four different adjectives

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Mon mari s'appelle Nguyen. Il est grand et brun. Il est sérieux, mais il est très drôle. Ma fille, Linh, est petite. Elle a six ans. Elle est un peu timide, mais elle est très gentille.
models.en: My husband's name is Nguyen. He's tall and dark-haired. He's serious, but he's very funny. My daughter, Linh, is little. She's six. She's a bit shy, but she's very kind.

summary:
- Describe people with [[être]] + adjective: [[Il est grand. Elle est gentille.]]
- Make adjectives agree: **-e** for feminine, **-s** for plural, plus [[gentille]] and [[sérieuse]]
- Ask [[Il est comment ?]] and soften or stress with [[un peu]] and [[très]]
- Know that most adjectives go after the noun ([[un ami drôle]]), but [[petit]], [[grand]], [[jeune]], [[beau]], [[bon]] go before
